Build a single-file interactive WebGPU page called "Plush Hammerhead".

Page: an editorial layout with a big two-line title "Plush / Hammerhead.", a warm studio-grey background, a control panel on the right, live readouts and collapsible technical notes. English UI.

The toy: a plush hammerhead shark. It has a wide, flat hammer-shaped head (cephalofoil) whose ends sweep back a little, with a shallow notch at the middle of the front edge. A glass eye sits on each tip of the hammer, looking out sideways. It has a tall sickle-shaped dorsal fin, two pectoral fins and a tail with a long upper lobe and a small lower one. A cream belly panel is sewn on below a seam along each flank, with embroidered gill lines. A smiling mouth is cut in under the hammer, lined with felt and set with soft white felt teeth; its lower jaw swings open on a hinge.

Simulation:
- Body, hammer and fins are one signed distance field filled with a soft-body XPBD lattice: shape-matched hexahedral cells and tetrahedral volume preservation. It is skinned to a high-res surface-nets mesh.
- It swims with a travelling S-wave that bends the cells' rest shapes side to side, more toward the tail, and steers by turning its head, the body curving into each turn.
- Fur is drawn as alpha-to-coverage shells over minky pile. The pile lags behind each jiggle on a spring and can be combed.

Behaviour:
- It circles its space.
- Scan: it sweeps its hammer side to side over the floor the way real hammerheads hunt. It also does this on its own now and then, and a little while hunting.
- Feed drops in a felt fish: it turns, closes in faster, opens wide and snaps it up.
- Dash is a burst of fast tail beats; Chomp opens the mouth and snaps it shut.
- Grab it by the tail and it thrashes; let go and it shoots off.
- Boop the middle of the hammer with the finger and it wriggles and blushes.

Tools: Hand, Finger, Comb.

Controls:
- Buttons: Feed, Dash, Scan, Chomp, Smooth fur, Reset, Pause.
- Toggles: Circle, quarter speed, Mesh.
- Sliders: Stuffing, Pile, Tail beat.
- Three fabrics: Bronze, Lagoon, Sunset.
- Readouts: mass, volume, beats per minute, fish eaten.
- Phone layout with a stacked panel.

Create a 15-second ultra-realistic Japanese home video, casually recorded today by a friend using an old second-hand consumer MiniDV camcorder from the early 2000s. Capture a sweet, spontaneous weekend shopping date between a young Japanese couple at a busy suburban Japanese shopping mall, with imperfect framing, natural interactions, and authentic everyday behavior.

CHARACTERS: @image1 is the woman and @image2 is her boyfriend. Use each sheet only for that person's face, hair, outfit and body proportions - never copy the sheets' layout, gray background or title text. The woman is a young Japanese woman in her early 20s with long dark-brown hair in soft loose waves and see-through bangs, natural light makeup, small pearl stud earrings, a dusty-lavender short-sleeve ankle-length maxi dress with a loose relaxed silhouette, white low-top canvas sneakers, and a small black leather crossbody bag. Her boyfriend is a young Japanese man in his early 20s with slightly messy soft black mushroom-cut hair, an oversized plain white short-sleeve T-shirt, loose beige wide-leg trousers, black low-top canvas sneakers, and a simple black wristwatch. He is about a head taller than her. Maintain consistent faces, outfits, and body proportions throughout. Only these two people are the couple; nobody else in the mall looks like them.

STORY:

The couple walks hand in hand through a crowded mall walkway on a weekend while the camera follows them from behind; she playfully pokes his arm and he laughs and dodges. They step into a lifestyle goods shop with a wall of colorful plush toys. She excitedly picks up an oversized brown teddy bear and hugs it tightly with both arms. He jokingly holds a tiny white stuffed rabbit right next to his face with a serious "cool" pose, and she bursts out laughing and says in Japanese: "Look, it's huge!" He answers: "I'll take this side.".

Carrying their plush toys in a paper shopping bag, they stop in front of a large mirror on a mall pillar. She pulls him close and takes a mirror selfie with a small old silver compact digital camera while he makes a goofy face behind her.

Next, they share one soft-serve ice cream cone while walking through the mall. She takes a lick, offers it to him, and laughs when he gets a little ice cream on the corner of his lip. She says softly in Japanese: "You've got something on you" and gently wipes it away with her finger as he smiles shyly.

They step into an old-fashioned mall elevator, still holding the shopping bag with the plush toys. Just before the doors close, he leans down and gives her a brief, sweet kiss. She smiles bashfully at the camera as the elevator doors slide shut, ending the recording abruptly.

CAMERA & FOOTAGE: Authentic early-2000s MiniDV footage in 16:9, handheld shake, imperfect framing, accidental zooms, autofocus hunting, exposure fluctuations, slightly faded colors, soft digital detail, mild compression noise, and natural motion blur. The camera behaves like a friend casually filming them, sometimes reacting late, briefly losing the action behind passing shoppers, then finding them again. No polished cinematography or smooth tracking shots. The people move continuously and naturally the whole time - never frozen, never a still image.

SETTING: A busy Japanese suburban shopping mall on a weekend afternoon, wide walkways, fashion and lifestyle shops, a shop with a wall of plush toys, large pillar mirrors, a soft-serve ice cream stand, an older stainless-steel elevator, fluorescent and skylight lighting, and Japanese shoppers and families passing naturally in the background.

AUDIO: Natural mall chatter, footsteps, Japanese shop announcements, shop ambience, a camera shutter click, paper shopping bag rustle, laughter, an elevator chime and the doors closing, and quiet spontaneous Japanese conversation. Only three short spoken lines: her "Look, it's huge!", his "I'll take this side.", and her "You've got something on you". Their lips move in sync with their words. No background music or narration.

REALISM & CONTINUITY: Natural couple chemistry, shy smiles, playful teasing, believable hand movements, realistic ice cream interaction, consistent character identities, and present-day Japanese surroundings. The couple keeps the paper shopping bag with the plush toys from the shop onward. The final kiss is brief and affectionate. The entire video must feel like a genuine personal memory recorded on an old camcorder, not a staged production. No text, no subtitles, no logos, no watermark.

Using Blender through Blender MCP, make a game-ready 3D model of the straw training dummy in the attached image. Work directly in Blender: build, look at the result, compare it with the reference and fix it. Match the reference as closely as you can: shape, proportions, materials and colours.

Requirements:
Real-world scale: about 1.85 m tall in total. Origin at the bottom centre of the post.
Up to 15,000 triangles in total.
Textures up to 2048 px: base colour, normal, roughness. Transparency is allowed for straw.
Ready to place in a realistic tropical-island shooter game.

Parts (separate named objects, so they can break off in the game):
"head" (with its burlap cloth), pivot at the base of the neck;
"arm_left" and "arm_right" (the bamboo pole split in two at the body), each with its pivot where it meets the body;
"body": everything else (post, straw body, rope, scarf) as one object.
Close the surfaces where parts meet: no holes visible when the head or an arm is gone.

Output:
One .glb file with all parts and textures embedded.
The .blend file.
A front view and a three-quarter view render on a plain background, so the result can be compared with the reference.
